questions.q: The Kalman gain K tends to 1 when:
options: The measurement is more precise than the prediction
Always
There are no measurements
The process model is accurate and the noise is small
questions.explain: K = P⁻/(P⁻+R): a small R → trust the measurement.

options: A new parameter
The measurement minus the prediction
The covariance
The process noise in the prediction step

questions.q: What happens when XKF4.SP > 1 in ArduPilot?
options: The position is accepted
The position is rejected by the gate
The EKF is reset and fully reinitialized
GPS is lost
questions.explain: SP is the ratio of the innovation to the allowed one (the square root of the test ratio); >1 means rejected.

questions.q: What does a long (10 s) barometer outlier do to a 1D filter with a gate?
options: The gate widens over time and lets everything through
Rejected at first, then the estimate "drifts off"
The filter stops
Nothing
questions.explain: Gates protect against short outliers, not against a systematic error.

questions.q: What is a lane in EKF3?
options: A GPS type
An EKF core for its own IMU
A flight mode
The gyro filter's frequency band
questions.explain: XKF4.PI is the index of the active core.

questions.q: How many states does EKF3 have?
questions.explain: Quaternion, velocity, position, gyro and accel bias, earth and body magnetic field, wind.

questions.q: What does a large R for a measurement mean?
options: The filter blindly follows the sensor
The model is considered inaccurate
The filter step becomes larger
The filter trusts this sensor less
questions.explain: R is the variance of the measurement noise: the larger it is, the smaller K and the measurement's weight.

questions.q: Why does the EKF account for sensor delays?
options: To call the firmware less often
To reduce the number of states
The EKF does not account for delays
The measurement belongs to a past moment, not the current one
questions.explain: The filter matches the measurement with the state at the time of measurement; otherwise it introduces an error.
